hypotheses.note: 0 < α, α ≠ 2π, E^{n+2}_α = Γ_1\(𝔻_∞ × E) of ex:conical (cone angle α, DEC-47), E any finite-dimensional Euclidean space, G = IsomPlus E

hypotheses.paper: the covering endowed with the singular Euclidean metric dr²+r²dθ²+Σdz_i² in cylindrical coordinates
hypotheses.note: a mathlib Bundle.RiemannianMetric (GX.tameCylMetric) on the tangent bundle of the cylindrical coordinate domain {r>0} ⊆ ℝ×ℝ×E, with coordinate expression ρ²+r²φ²+‖ζ‖² and analytic coefficients; the coordinates GX.cylCoord are an open embedding onto the regular part {r>0} of the cover; the metric equals D^*⟨·,·⟩ (locally Euclidean, D a local homeomorphism there) and is degenerate at r=0

labels.notes: The metric sentence is certified, not read: the paper writes the metric in cylindrical coordinates of the cover, and that is exactly what is built — a genuine mathlib Riemannian metric on the coordinate domain (an open subset of a vector space, hence a smooth manifold), the coordinates identifying it with the regular part of the cover, plus Euclideanity (g = D^*eucl) and singularity (degenerate at r=0). Mathlib's Riemannian metrics live on tangent bundles of smooth manifolds; the cover Susp ℝ × E is only a topological space in GX, which is why the metric is carried by its regular part through the coordinates — where the paper itself writes it. Nothing beyond the coordinate claim is asserted by the paper (no continuous extension of g to r=0, no metric-space structure on the cover).

kb_proposals: Mathlib HAS a usable Riemannian metric (Bundle.RiemannianMetric, Topology/VectorBundle/Riemannian.lean): on an open subset U : Opens F of a normed space it is a structure on TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, F) : U → Type with fields inner/symm/pos/continuousAt/isVonNBounded; imports Mathlib.Topology.VectorBundle.Riemannian + Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.Tangent suffice (GX.tameCylMetric).

innerSL ℝ has type E →L⋆[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ; to add it to ordinary →L[ℝ] bilinear forms, re-type it through a def `: E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ := innerSL ℝ` (defeq) with an rfl apply lemma (GX.tameInnerCLM); simp lemmas about innerSL then do not fire, use the apply lemma.

At this pin, NormedAddCommGroup ((ℝ × E) →L[ℝ] (ℝ × E) →L[ℝ] ℝ) FAILS to synthesize (while E →L E →L ℝ succeeds); avoid statements needing a norm on such bilinear-map spaces (state smoothness coefficientwise).
IsVonNBounded on a TangentSpace fibre: `change` the set to one of the model vector space, then NormedSpace.isVonNBounded_iff and a closed ball.
